 Advertisement Medication used to treat blood pressure recalled over possible metal contamination, company says
 Advertisement Updated: 7:15 AM CST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Caitlyn Scott Digital Producer Medication used to treat blood pressure recalled over possible metal contamination, company says
 Updated: 7:15 AM CST Nov 17, 2026 Editorial Standards ⓘ Caitlyn Scott Digital Producer A pharmaceutical company has issued a voluntary nationwide recall after it said a lot of medication used to typically treat blood pressure may be contaminated with metal. 
 Breckenridge Pharmaceutical Inc. issued a voluntary recall for one lot of 60 mg propranolol hydrochloride extended-release capsules. The effected lot, PK25110035, has an expiration date labeled as May 2029. 
 Advertisement The company said the medication was distributed nationwide to wholesalers and pharmacies between Oct. 26, 2026, and Nov. 4, 2026. 
 Related video: How to stay ahead of recalls 
 "Use of product from the affected lot could potentially cause lacerations of soft tissues in the oral cavity, esophagus, stomach, or intestine," the company said on its website. "The affected lot shared intermediate material suspected to be the source of metal contamination identified in a separate lot that was not released to market."
 Breckenridge Pharmaceutical said it is not aware of any adverse events assessed to be related to the recall.
 Consumers are asked to stop use of the product from the recalled lot and contact their doctor or healthcare provider for medical advice and replacement instructions. The company also advised consumers to return any unused portion of the affected product to the pharmacy where it was picked up.
 The company also urged wholesalers, pharmacies, and other retailers to check their inventories. 
 According to the Cleveland Clinic, propranolol hydrochloride extended-release capsules help to treat many conditions, including high blood pressure and heart disease. The clinic says the medication works by lowering blood pressure and heart rate, making it easier to pump blood through the rest of the body.
